title: The Wise Men of Chelm and the Ox That Was All the Best Bits
summary: In Chelm they cooked a huge ox for Shabbat, and three rich men took the best piece, the best seat and the biggest honor for themselves. Everyone wanted "the best," and the quarrel swelled up like a balloon! Then three judges came from far away and gave a strange and funny ruling in which everything is the best. A rhyming story based on a folk tale of the Wise Men of Chelm.
pages:
In Chelm they cooked a giant ox in honor of Shabbat,
and the rich men took the best of it — the best of all they got!
The other Chelmites peeked, and their tummies rumbled: "Grrrr, grrrr!"

In the study house, too, everyone wanted the best — by the eastern wall, the warmest and coziest spot,
and the important men sat there like kings, on cushioned chairs, the best seats of the lot.
"I want the best!"
"Not you! Stay back with the rest!"

And when they read from the Torah — everyone jumped up: "I'm the third!"
And another shouted, "No! Me — or at least the sixth, that's my word!"
"I want the best!"
"Not you! Stay back with the rest!"

And the quarrel grew like a balloon, every Shabbat — a bit more, and more, and more,
till all the Chelmites turned their backs on each other — and fell silent, a heavy silence like never before.
"I want the best!"
"Not you! Stay back with the rest!"

The elders said, "Our town will split in two!
Let's invite three wise judges from far away, from beyond the sky so blue!"

Three judges came in a wagon pulled by a donkey, tall and straight,
with tall hats, round glasses, and a long scroll — serious and great.

They listened to everyone, all day and all through the night,
and scratched their beards, and whispered, and wrote a list — long, long, long, out of sight.

The next day Yokel knocked: TOK! And all of Chelm listened, quiet and still,
and the judge proclaimed: "Hear this! From now on, the whole ox — is breast and shank, the best bits, every one!
The whole synagogue — is the eastern wall! And every Torah reading — is third and sixth, for everyone!"

The Chelmites looked at their plates — and everything was "breast and shank,"
and they were happy, and took a big breath, and burst out laughing — they had the judges to thank.
"I want the best!" said one — and nobody said, "Stay back with the rest!"

Everyone sat facing east, shoulder to shoulder, the children in the very first row,
and they ate a whole ox, all breast and shank, with joy and singing, all aglow.

They read from the Torah: "Third!" — and everyone stood up, like a wave in the sea,
"I'm the third!" — and that was perfectly fine, and the fairest for all it could be.

And on Friday, in Chelm, they cooked a giant ox in honor of Shabbat,
and everyone — with no exception — got the best of it, the best of all they got!
"I want the best!" — "Me too!" — "Me too!"
